reference_meta.coverage_note: Woods translates all three layers, so the reference covers the whole page, arranged in Woods's order (sūtra 48, bhāṣya 48, Vācaspati on 48, sūtra 49, bhāṣya 49, Vācaspati on 49) rather than the page's (sūtra+bhāṣya above, Vācaspati below). The bhāṣya on 49 continues past the page break to its end ('...takes his recreation as having mastery.') as boundary context; the Vācaspati on 49 is cut exactly where the page ends ('This same he explains by the words «essence of all things.»'). Woods's footnotes and markers dropped; guillemet quote marks around the last lemma restored from OCR '^'. Some OCR noise left as fetched (e.g. 'rnadhupratika', '<one who knows alb'). The variant-reading apparatus has no reference.

reference_meta.title: Lotus Sutra
reference_meta.located: ch. 13 Sukhavihāraparivarta, opening prose (Kern ch. XIII 'Peaceful Life', SBE 21 pp. 262-264): from Mañjuśrī's question through the 'proper sphere' and the start of the first proper sphere (page ends mid-sentence at 'sa nāntaśo dharmasaṃrāgeṇāpi dharmaṃ', = Kern 'he does not do so by passionate attachment to the law')
reference_meta.coverage_note: Reference covers the whole page from the chapter opening; it continues past the page's last (broken) sentence to the end of that paragraph ('...first proper sphere of a Bodhisattva Mahasattva.') as boundary context. The archive.org OCR garbles diacritics (e.g. 'Mazgusri', 'Ma#gusri', 'Mahdsattva' for Mañgusrî/Mahâsattva, 'Aarakas', 'KAndalas'); these are left as fetched; only Kern's footnote markers and one stray quote mark were dropped.

reference_meta.title: Mahabharata
reference_meta.located: Ādiparvan adhyāya 227 (Calcutta numbering) last ślokas (Arjuna repels Indra's second rain of stones; Mandara peak shattered) and adhyāya 228 ślokas 1–~23 (rout of the forest creatures, Krishna's discus, the bodiless voice about Takshaka and Nara-Nārāyaṇa, Indra returns to heaven); running ślokas c. 8277–8296; printed page 301
reference_meta.coverage_note: Ganguli's numbering is offset: Calcutta adhy. 227 = Ganguli Adi Parva Section CCXXIX (end), Calcutta adhy. 228 = Ganguli Section CCXXX. Context added: one sentence before (Indra's first stone shower, last śloka of the previous page) and one after (the gods follow Indra). The Section CCXXX sub-heading '(Khandava-daha Parva continued)' was dropped; translator's footnotes: none in this span. Ganguli's text has a misprint 'moved able like death itself' — kept verbatim.

reference_meta.title: Gita Govinda
reference_meta.located: Sarga 7: closing signature stanza (v. 8) of song 14 (aṣṭapadī 'smara-samarocita-viracita-veśā', the Haririmitacampakaśekhara prabandha), then the following śloka 'virahapāṇḍu-murāri-mukhāmbuja-dyutir ayaṃ' (Rādhā to the moon)
reference_meta.coverage_note: Arnold is a free verse paraphrase. Mapping: stanza 'Till at length, a fatal victress ... my Pain!' = song 14 v. 7 (context, not on the page); the italic 'But may Radha's fond annoy ... evil age' = song 14 v. 8 (the Jayadeva signature couplet on the page); 'O Moon! (she sang) ... I have striven in vain.' = the śloka virahapāṇḍu... (on the page; Arnold expands 2 Sanskrit lines to 6 English lines and adds the apostrophe to Krishna). Reference stops before Arnold's next line, which opens song 15. Italic underscores removed. The commentaries (about 95% of the page) have no reference; consider this a weak page for the A/B because the root text is short.

reference_meta.title: कथासरित्सागर (Kathāsaritsāgara)
reference_meta.located: Śaśāṅkavatīlambaka taraṅga 32 (ādita 100) vv. 49–58 (end of Vikramakesarin's tale; close of the Vetāla frame) and taraṅga 33 (ādita 101) vv. 1–12 (maṅgala; Mṛgāṅkadatta crosses the desert and sees the lake); printed page 536
reference_meta.coverage_note: Tawney's chapter numbering is one lower here: Sanskrit ādita taraṅga 101 = Tawney Chapter C; the end of taraṅga 100 is the end of Tawney's Chapter XCIX. Context added: one sentence before v. 49 (the corpse and summoning, v. 47–48) and one after v. 12 (the lake's breadth, v. 13). Tawney's separately printed 'Note' on the number of Vetala tales (between the chapters) is a translator's note and is omitted, as are his footnotes and markers. Text collated from two archive.org OCRs of the 1880–84 Calcutta edition to fix OCR errors; Tawney's accents/diacritics flattened (Mrigánkadatta -> Mrigankadatta etc.); 'this this' is in the print (both OCRs).

reference_meta.title: The Cloud Messenger
reference_meta.located: Uttaramegha: end of Mallinātha's commentary on v. 40 (this edition's numbering), v. 41 'tām āyuṣman mama ca vacanād' (whole, with commentary), and the first two pādas of v. 42 'aṅgenāṅgaṃ pratanu tanunā'. = Ryder's Latter Cloud stanzas XXXVII (end) - XXXIX
reference_meta.coverage_note: Reference covers the root text only: XXXVIII = v. 41 (whole, on page); XXXIX = v. 42 (only its first two pādas are on the page; the rest is on the next page); XXXVII = v. 40 (context: on this page only the tail of its commentary appears). Ryder's italic marginal analyses (his own additions, drawn from Mallinātha) were removed, as were the stanza-gloss lines; his Roman stanza numbers are kept. Ryder renders each 4-line Sanskrit stanza as a rhymed 5-line English stanza and is free in places. Mallinātha's commentary (most of the page) has no reference.

reference_meta.title: कुमारसम्भव (Kumārasambhava)
reference_meta.located: Canto VII, verses 28-30 (whole)
reference_meta.coverage_note: Reference covers the three root verses only; Mallinātha's commentary and the variant footnotes have no reference. Griffith's 1879 version is a free rhymed paraphrase, not verse-for-verse. Mapping: 'Then at her mother's hest ... reverend feet' = VII.27 (context); 'They raised the maiden ... perfect bliss' = VII.28; 'Well-pleased HIMÁLAYA ... monarch's state' = VII.29; 'Meanwhile by heavenly matrons' care ... the bridegroom wore' = VII.30; 'He laid his hand ... wish to wear' = VII.31 (context; Griffith's couplet is loose). PG markup ['S]IVA rendered as ŚIVA.

reference_meta.title: श्रीमद्वाल्मीकिरामायण (Rāmāyaṇa)
reference_meta.located: Yuddhakāṇḍa sarga 39 (Laṅkādarśana) vv. 17–29 (end of sarga) and sarga 40 (Rāvaṇa–Sugrīva duel) vv. 1–7; printed page 730
reference_meta.coverage_note: Dutt's prose = Yuddha Kandam Section XXXIX end and Section XL opening. Context added: one sentence before (v. 16, the dust cloud) and one after (sarga 40 v. 8, Sugriva bounds to the gateway). Dutt's text gives Lanka as 'ten yojanas in width and twenty in length' whereas this edition reads 100 x 30 yojanas (v. 21). Text taken from two archive.org OCRs of the same 1893 print, used to correct single-witness OCR errors (e.g. 'moiinlains'); diacritics flattened (Rāma -> Rama, chāmaras -> chamaras), 'yoyanas' kept as both OCRs read it; translator's footnotes (on Trikuta, Vishnu's middle step) and footnote markers dropped. Section XXXIX heading is not on this page.

reference_meta.title: महाभारत (Mahābhārata) — BORI Critical Edition
reference_meta.located: Karṇaparvan 8.22.58–61 (end of adhyāya 22: Karṇa's boast; Duryodhana grants the carts and cars; turns to Śalya) and 8.23.1–2ab (Duryodhana humbly approaches Śalya); printed page 174; edition's concordance line: Calcutta 8.1318, Bombay 8.31.68, Kumbhakonam 8.22.72
reference_meta.coverage_note: Ganguli follows the vulgate (Bombay/Calcutta) numbering: BORI 8.22 = Ganguli Karna Parva Section XXXI, BORI 8.23 = Ganguli Section XXXII (offset of 9 adhyāyas here). Context added: one sentence before 8.22.58 ('Thou wilt then see...') and the rest of Duryodhana's vocative string after 8.23.2ab (to '...hostile troops with fear,'). Ganguli's 'The very gods and Asuras are not able to advance against me... of human origin?' after 8.22.58 has no counterpart on this page (vulgate-only lines, not in the critical text); Ganguli also expands 8.22.59–60 (cars with steeds, vulturine feathers). The critical apparatus has no reference. The Project Gutenberg text prints section headings as bare numerals ('32' = Section XXXII), kept as printed.

reference_meta.title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता (Bhagavad Gita, 1492 MS)

Djvu OCR artefacts normalised: 'Vi^vas' → 'Visvas', 'A^vins' → 'Asvins', 'Vish;Ai'/'Vish;ai' → 'Vishnu', 'Dhr/tarash/ra' → 'Dhritarâshtra', 'Dro;/a' → 'Drona', 'recog-- nise' rejoined. reference_meta.title: Commentary on the Brahma Sutras
reference_meta.located: Brahmasūtra III.3.14 (Śaṅkara numbering; adhikaraṇa 7), siddhānta part of the bhāṣya from 'puruṣa eva hy ebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ paraḥ', then sūtra III.3.15 'ātmaśabdāc ca' and its bhāṣya up to 'evam anekaprakāra-' (page break); below, Bhāmatī on 14-15 and Nyāyanirṇaya on 14-15
reference_meta.coverage_note: Commentary identified as Śaṅkara's (not Rāmānuja's): the header reads ब्रह्मसूत्रभाष्यम् and the running heads elsewhere name भाष्यरत्नप्रभा-भामती-न्यायनिर्णयव्याख्यात्रयोपेतम्, sub-commentaries on Śaṅkara; the wording matches Śaṅkara's bhāṣya, so Thibaut SBE 38 is the matching translation. The reference covers only the Śaṅkara bhāṣya portion; it starts at the siddhānta ('To this we reply as follows. We must assume...'), one sentence before the page's first words, and continues past the page break in sūtra 15 to the end of that bhāṣya ('...relation of the senses, objects, and so on).') as boundary context. The Bhāmatī and Nyāyanirṇaya (about 75% of the page) have no public-domain English and no reference. OCR artefacts in transliterations ('Ka///aka', 'Vish/m', 'Vish;/u') left as fetched.

reference_meta.title: Kāmasūtra of Vātsyāyana with Yaśodhara's Jayamaṅgalā commentary
reference_meta.translator: Richard F. Burton & F. F. Arbuthnot
reference_meta.style_note: Victorian paraphrase that merges and reorders sūtras; sense is close but not a sūtra-by-sūtra crib
reference_meta.located: Book V (Pāradārika), ch. 2 closing verse 27 and colophon; ch. 3 (Bhāvaparīkṣā) sūtras 1-3 and the opening of sūtra 4
reference_meta.coverage_note: Reference covers the root text only; the Jayamaṅgalā commentary and the two colophons have no reference. Burton renders freely: verse 27 is folded into the prose paragraph ending ch. II; sūtra 1 = 'When a man is trying ... acts as follows'; sūtra 2 = 'If she listens to him ... go-between'; sūtra 3 (rejects the approach yet meets him again: of two minds, win her gradually) has no clean separate rendering; 'If she meets him once ... better dressed' corresponds to sūtra 4, which the page only begins. The final sentence ('A woman who lets a man make up to her ...') is either Burton's loose rendering of sūtra 3 or the following sūtra; it is kept as the boundary.
reference_meta.page_content: Root text: closing śloka 27 of V.2, the chapter colophon, and V.3 sūtras 1-3 plus the first words of sūtra 4; each followed by Jayamaṅgalā commentary (commentary and colophons are roughly 55-60% of the page; the reference covers the root text, about 40%).
reference_meta.source: Richard F. Burton & F. F. Arbuthnot (with Bhagavanlal Indrajit and Shivaram Parashuram Bhide), The Kama Sutra of Vatsyayana, Kama Shastra Society, 1883 (Project Gutenberg #27827), Part V ch. II end and ch. III opening
